title: Counterpoint: an 8.6-Gen line cuts the cost of an 11.1" iPad Pro OLED panel by 39% compared to a 6-Gen line
content: Counterpoint Research released its latest IT Display Cost Report, which analyzes the manufacturing costs of OLED and LCD panels for tablets, laptops and monitors from 2024 to 2030. According to Counterpoint, an 11.1-inch iPad Pro OLED panel produced at an 8.6-Gen fab costs about 39% less to make in 2026 than the same panel produced at a 6-Gen fab.

title: BOE reportedly in talks to acquire Visionox
content: According to a report from Korea, BOE is in talks to acquire Chinese AMOLED producer Visionox. BOE initially looked to buy one of Visionox's OLED production lines, but the talks have since expanded to a possible takeover of the entire company.

title: Samsung Display makes its biggest microLED move yet, to acquire a 9.1% stake in ams OSRAM for $230 million
content: Samsung Display announced that it has signed an agreement to acquire a 9.1% stake in ams OSRAM for around $230 million, which will make it the European LED and sensor maker's largest shareholder. title: OLED Emitter Systems, Part 3: TADF - the generation that became a supporting actor
content: The OLED emitter is the material at the heart of every pixel, the organic molecule that actually turns electricity into light. Everything else in the stack exists to deliver charge to it. The emitter is a key part in determining the display's color, efficiency and lifetime.

title: Analysis: Nvidia leadership settled, but US export rules still cloud outlook for Taiwan server makers
content: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO has eased uncertainty over the chipmaker's leadership, but Taiwan's AI server manufacturers are more concerned about whether Washington will revise its new AI chip export rules.

title: Maintenance and component demand lift profits across Taiwan's aerospace supply chain

Although uncertainty over Boeing's production ramp-up schedule has delayed new aircraft deliveries, maintenance demand has remained unaffected. title: Canon unveils first new ArF dry scanner in 24 years
content: Canon will begin taking orders in early December for its first new argon fluoride (ArF) dry lithography scanner in 24 years, returning to a market it exited in 2007 as demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment grows.

title: Congo halts cobalt exports, but CATL may see limited impact for now
content: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has announced a suspension of cobalt exports to stabilize prices amid weak global demand. The development may have a limited impact on electric battery makers like CATL due to the emergence of low-cobalt technologies and alternative sources of the metal, although the DRC's market dominance still makes it difficult for cobalt buyers to replace.

title: Memory surge weighs on Japan's mobile market outlook through 2027
content: Tight memory supply and broader inflation are squeezing Japan's mobile phone market. According to Japanese market research firm MM Research Institute, total handset shipments in Japan fell 9.2% year-over-year to 12.889 million units in the first half of fiscal 2026 (April–September 2026). This was the second-lowest first-half volume recorded since fiscal 2000, trailing only the first half of fiscal 2023.
